basic_info.name: alignDRAW 10-Year Anniversary (Fellowship.xyz)
basic_info.location: Art Basel Miami Beach (2024), Worcester Art Museum, Massachusetts (2025) [uncertain], London (Fellowship.xyz HQ)

practice_description.medium: Publication (large-format book), exhibition, film, AI-generated imagery, critical essays
practice_description.practice_summary: A large-format book and exhibition programme celebrating the 10th anniversary of Elman Mansimov's alignDRAW (2015) -- the first neural network system to generate images from text descriptions. Positions this engineering milestone as a pivotal art historical event through critical essays, new model outputs, and contextual framing.
practice_description.methodology: Fellowship.xyz commissioned essays from art historians, critics, and practitioners to contextualise alignDRAW within art history and technology discourse. The project reframes a machine learning research paper (published on arXiv in 2015 by Mansimov, Srivastava, and others at the University of Toronto) as an art historical origin point for text-to-image generation. The book includes essays by Mat Dryhurst, Lev Manovich, Eva Jager, Shana Lopes, and Darius Himes, alongside reproductions of original alignDRAW outputs and new generations from the model. An accompanying interview film documents Mansimov's perspective.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: alignDRAW 10-Year directly models the kind of field intelligence A(DAI) produces -- identifying art historical significance in technical research and building canonical narratives that bridge engineering and cultural production. It demonstrates how arXiv papers and research outputs can be primary material for artistic and curatorial work.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. The project treats a machine learning model's outputs as art historical artefacts -- the blurry, early text-to-image generations become substrates for critical analysis and exhibition. The original alignDRAW model itself is framed as a creative instrument whose outputs are raw material for art historical canonisation.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes. The project is fundamentally relational -- it maps connections between computer science research (University of Toronto, arXiv), art history (Manovich's analysis), curatorial practice (Fellowship's framing), practitioner discourse (Dryhurst's essay on where 'glimpses of the world to come' emerge), and institutional legitimacy (museum exhibitions).
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Partially. The project recomposes a 2015 research paper through 2024-2025 critical lenses, demonstrating how meaning accumulates over time. The exhibition programme evolves across venues. However, the book itself is a fixed publication.

works.title: alignDRAW 10-Year Anniversary Book
works.description: Large-format publication featuring essays by Lev Manovich (media theory, art history context), Mat Dryhurst (arXiv as site of cultural production), Eva Jager (institutional and curatorial perspective), Shana Lopes (art history), and Darius Himes (photography and image-making). Includes original alignDRAW outputs from 2015 and new generations.
works.relevance: Directly models A(DAI)'s approach: treating technical research as field intelligence and building relational narratives that connect engineering, art, and culture.

works.title: alignDRAW Exhibition at Art Basel Miami Beach
works.description: Exhibition presenting the alignDRAW book and related materials at Art Basel Miami Beach, positioning the project within the premier international art fair context.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how field intelligence (a 2015 arXiv paper) can be exhibited in the highest tier of the art market, validating the canonisation methodology.

works.title: alignDRAW at Worcester Art Museum
works.description: Museum exhibition bringing the alignDRAW project into an institutional collection context, bridging from art fair to museum.
works.relevance: Shows the institutional pipeline from research artefact to art fair to museum collection -- a canonisation pathway A(DAI) can learn from.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: The project treats canonisation itself as a creative act -- the protocol of selecting, framing, and contextualising a technical milestone as art history is the artistic intervention. Fellowship's methodology (commissioning critical essays, producing publication, exhibiting at art fairs and museums) is a canonisation protocol that transforms engineering research into cultural artefact.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: A canonisation pipeline: identify overlooked technical milestone, commission interdisciplinary critical essays, produce high-quality publication, exhibit at art fairs, place in museum context. This is a replicable system for bridging engineering research and art history.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: The original alignDRAW research paper is open access (arXiv). The book and exhibition operate commercially through Fellowship.xyz. The project contributes to commons knowledge by making visible a foundational technical-artistic milestone. Mat Dryhurst's essay specifically argues for recognising arXiv and open research as sites of cultural production -- advocating for the commons value of open scientific publishing.

governance_model.governance_detail: Directed by Fellowship.xyz (Alejandro Cartagena, Chadwick Tyler). Curatorial and editorial decisions made by Fellowship with input from commissioned essayists. Elman Mansimov is credited as the original researcher. Standard gallery/publisher governance model.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Essayists commissioned and credited. Mansimov participates as interview subject and is positioned as originating researcher. Standard publishing consent frameworks.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Collective authorship across multiple registers: Mansimov as original researcher, five essayists as critical interpreters, Fellowship.xyz as curatorial frame, and the alignDRAW model itself as an authorial agent whose outputs are exhibited. The project explicitly questions what authorship means when a neural network generates images.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: The book is a fixed publication. The exhibition programme has a defined touring schedule. However, the project's conceptual contribution -- framing a 2015 arXiv paper as an art historical event -- creates a durable canonical claim that will persist and be cited.

data_materiality.data_sources: Original alignDRAW model outputs (2015), new generations from the model, Mansimov's research paper and documentation, critical essays, interview footage, art historical and media theory analysis (Manovich), curatorial and institutional framing.
data_materiality.data_provenance: The original alignDRAW research was published openly on arXiv. Model outputs are generated from the original system. Critical essays are commissioned original writing. Interview content is consented. All sources are transparent and attributed.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: alignDRAW was itself an early text-to-image system operating in a shared text-image embedding space -- the model learned to generate images from text descriptions by aligning textual and visual representations. The 10-Year project is thus directly about the history and significance of embedding space navigation as creative practice.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes. The project spans text (essays, research paper), image (AI-generated outputs), film (interview), and physical publication. The original alignDRAW system was itself a multimodal text-to-image system.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Exhibited as a physical publication and gallery display at Art Basel Miami Beach and Worcester Art Museum. The book functions as a portable exhibition object. Online presence through fellowship.xyz. The project bridges art fair booth, museum gallery, and printed page.

interoperability.composability: Moderate. The essays and critical frameworks are composable -- they can be cited, built upon, and applied to other contexts. The canonisation methodology is replicable. The original alignDRAW model outputs are visual artefacts that could be incorporated into other compositions.
interoperability.technical_openness: The original alignDRAW research is open (arXiv). The publication is commercial. The critical frameworks circulate through the essays and can be freely referenced.

technical_approach.stack: The original alignDRAW: attention-based recurrent neural network for text-to-image generation (2015, University of Toronto). The 10-Year project: print publishing, exhibition design, film production, web platform (fellowship.xyz)

network_position.scene_affiliation: AI art history and canon formation, Fellowship.xyz network, Art Basel / international art fair circuit, academic media theory (Manovich), Serpentine Arts Technologies (Eva Jager connection), AI art practitioner discourse (Dryhurst), museum collections (Worcester Art Museum), photography and image theory (Darius Himes)
network_position.connections: Fellowship.xyz (producer), Mat Dryhurst (essayist -- connects to Holly Herndon, Interdependence, Spawning AI), Eva Jager (essayist -- connects to Serpentine Arts Technologies, FAE reports), Lev Manovich (essayist -- connects to academic media theory), Elman Mansimov (original researcher, University of Toronto), Shana Lopes (art historian), Darius Himes (photography), Art Basel Miami Beach, Worcester Art Museum

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: alignDRAW 10-Year provides A(DAI) with: (1) a methodology for canonising technical research as art historical event -- directly applicable to A(DAI)'s field intelligence work; (2) Dryhurst's essay arguing that arXiv and engineering communities produce 'glimpses of the world to come' -- validating A(DAI)'s approach to scanning unconventional sources; (3) a model for how publication and exhibition can transform field intelligence into cultural artefact; (4) network connections to key figures (Dryhurst, Jager, Manovich) who are already in A(DAI)'s graph.
